supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Let $\mathcal H$ be a complex Hilbert space of finite dimension $d\ge1$, $H=H^*$ with energy unit J, $\hbar>0$ with unit J s, $\beta>0$ with unit J$^{-1}$, and let $\sigma=Z_\beta^{-1}e^{-\beta H}$ be the stationary Gibbs density from [[thm-qsm-dt-finite-unitary]]. Let $A=A^*$ and $B=B^*$ be matrices, let $T>0$ be finite in s, let $h:[0,T]\to\mathbb R$ be continuous, and let $\epsilon\in\mathbb R$ be dimensionless; $h(t)B$ has unit J. Put $U_0(t)=e^{-itH/\hbar}$ for time $t$ in s, $\alpha_t(A)=U_0(t)^*AU_0(t)$, and $B_t=\alpha_t(B)$. Let $W_\epsilon$ solve
$$W_\epsilon'(t)=\frac{i\epsilon h(t)}{\hbar}B_tW_\epsilon(t),\qquad W_\epsilon(0)=I,$$
and set $U_\epsilon(t)=U_0(t)W_\epsilon(t)$ and $\rho_I(t)=W_\epsilon(t)\sigma W_\epsilon(t)^*$. Then $U_\epsilon$ solves $i\hbar U_\epsilon'(t)=(H-\epsilon h(t)B)U_\epsilon(t)$, $U_\epsilon(0)=I$, and $\rho_\epsilon(t):=U_\epsilon(t)\sigma U_\epsilon(t)^*$ satisfies $\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_\epsilon(t)A)=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_I(t)\alpha_t(A))$. Define
$$R_{AB}(u)=\frac{i}{\hbar}\operatorname{Tr}\!\left(\sigma[\alpha_u(A),B]\right),\qquad C_T=\frac{2}{\hbar}\int_0^T|h(s)|\,\|B\|\,ds.$$
Then $W_\epsilon(t)$ is unitary and, for $0\le t\le T$,
$$\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_I(t)\alpha_t(A))=\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma\alpha_t(A))+\epsilon\int_0^t h(s)R_{AB}(t-s)\,ds+r_\epsilon(t),\qquad |r_\epsilon(t)|\le\|A\|\frac{(|\epsilon|C_T)^2e^{|\epsilon|C_T}}2.$$
The initial Gibbs matrix is fixed as $\epsilon$ varies. The result is an exact finite-time first variation with a controlled remainder, not a static derivative of a re-prepared Gibbs family. $C_T$ and $\epsilon$ are dimensionless, and $R_{AB}$ has units $[A][B]/(\mathrm J\,\mathrm s)$.

Fix either a finite open chain with sites $\{1,\ldots,L\}$, $L\ge2$, or a periodic chain with sites $\mathbb Z/L\mathbb Z$, $L\ge3$, and denote its site set by $\Lambda_L$. Let $\mathcal H_L$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space. For each site $j$, let $q_j=q_j^*$ be a bounded charge observable, with physical unit $\mathsf Q$. For each oriented nearest-neighbor bond $(j,j+1)$, let $h_{j,j+1}=h_{j,j+1}^*$ be an energy operator in joules. Require $[h_{k,k+1},q_j]=0$ whenever $j\notin\{k,k+1\}$, and require local charge conservation $[h_{j,j+1},q_j+q_{j+1}]=0$. On an open chain set $H_L=\sum_{j=1}^{L-1}h_{j,j+1}$; on a ring set $H_L=\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z/L\mathbb Z}h_{j,j+1}$ with periodic indices. For an open chain define the absent boundary currents $j_{0,1}=j_{L,L+1}=0$. Use $\hbar>0$ in joule-seconds. These finite local data may be realized on a tensor-product spin space or on a finite fixed-particle site space, provided the stated commutation conditions hold.

The oriented bond current from $j$ to $j+1$ is
$$j_{j,j+1}:=\frac{i}{\hbar}[h_{j,j+1},q_{j+1}].$$
It has unit $\mathsf Q\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$. The total current is the sum over existing bonds, $J_L:=\sum_{(j,j+1)}j_{j,j+1}$, and its Heisenberg evolution for $t\in\mathbb R$ is $J_L(t):=e^{iH_Lt/\hbar}J_Le^{-iH_Lt/\hbar}$. For finite inverse temperature $\beta>0$ in joules$^{-1}$, define $\rho_{\beta,L}:=e^{-\beta H_L}/\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta H_L})$ and $\omega_{\beta,L}(A):=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_{\beta,L}A)$. Write $J_L^\circ:=J_L-\omega_{\beta,L}(J_L)I$ and $J_L^\circ(t):=e^{iH_Lt/\hbar}J_L^\circ e^{-iH_Lt/\hbar}$. Define the real, connected, symmetrized correlation per site by
$$C_L(t):=\frac{1}{L}\operatorname{Re}\,\omega_{\beta,L}\!\left(J_L^\circ(t)J_L^\circ\right)=\frac{1}{2L}\omega_{\beta,L}\!\left(J_L^\circ(t)J_L^\circ+J_L^\circ J_L^\circ(t)\right).$$
The correlation has unit $\mathsf Q^2\,\mathrm{s}^{-2}$ per site.

This definition assigns no transport coefficient by itself. Any proposed finite-volume or thermodynamic transport quantity must additionally state its time cutoff, frequency regulator (for example $e^{-\eta t}$ with $\eta>0$ in seconds$^{-1}$), spatial normalization, and the exact order in which $L\to\infty$, the time cutoff tends to infinity, and any regulator is removed. Existence of those limits is not part of this definition.

derivations.claim: Since $h_{j,j+1}$ and $q_{j+1}$ are self-adjoint, $[h_{j,j+1},q_{j+1}]^*=-[h_{j,j+1},q_{j+1}]$. Thus $j_{j,j+1}=(i/\hbar)[h_{j,j+1},q_{j+1}]$ is self-adjoint.

The Heisenberg derivative is $\dot q_j=(i/\hbar)\sum_k[h_{k,k+1},q_j]$. By [A1], only the existing bonds immediately to the left and right of $j$ can contribute. The left contribution is $(i/\hbar)[h_{j-1,j},q_j]=j_{j-1,j}$ when that bond exists, and is zero by the open-boundary convention otherwise.

For the right contribution, [A2] gives $[h_{j,j+1},q_j]=-[h_{j,j+1},q_{j+1}]$, so $(i/\hbar)[h_{j,j+1},q_j]=-j_{j,j+1}$ when that bond exists. If it is absent at the open right endpoint, both terms are zero by convention.

Combining steps 1.2 and 1.3 proves $\dot q_j=j_{j-1,j}-j_{j,j+1}$. Summing over $j\in\Lambda_L$ cancels every existing open-chain or periodic bond once with each sign, so $\dot Q_L=0$, equivalently $[H_L,Q_L]=0$.

Under the finite-dimensional unitary dynamics of [[thm-qsm-dt-finite-unitary]], let $P_E$ be the orthogonal spectral projection of $H$ for its distinct energy $E$. For every density matrix $\rho$,

Use the following conventions on a complex inner-product space $H$ of dimension $D\geq1$, with inner product linear in its first argument. For an endomorphism $A$, define $\operatorname{Tr}A:=\sum_{j=1}^D\langle Ae_j,e_j\rangle$ in an orthonormal basis; step 3.1 proves basis independence. For any Hermitian $M$, its **positive spectral subspace** (called its positive support here) is $S_M:=\bigoplus_{\lambda>0}\ker(M-\lambda I)$; when $M\geq0$ this equals $(\ker M)^\perp$. Its support logarithm is $\log(M|_{S_M}):=\sum_{\lambda>0}(\log\lambda)P_\lambda|_{S_M}$, where $P_\lambda$ is the orthogonal projection onto that eigenspace. derivations.claim: In the classical alternative fix $T>0$ and use Lebesgue measure on $[0,T]$ for the Bochner integral. Each $J_n$ is a measurable simple function. Uniform continuity of $J$ on $[0,T]$ gives $\sup_{t\in[0,T]}\|J_n(t)-J(t)\|_2\to0$, and hence $\int_0^T\|J_n(t)-J(t)\|_2\,dt\to0$. Thus $J$ is strongly measurable (an almost-everywhere limit of measurable simple functions), and $\int_0^T\|J(t)\|_2\,dt<\infty$ because $J$ is bounded. By the definition of the Bochner integral as the $L^1$-norm limit of integrals of simple functions, $J$ is Bochner integrable. The Bochner integrals of $J_n$ are the left-endpoint Riemann sums for $J$; they converge both to the Bochner integral by the $L^1$ approximation and to the norm-Riemann integral by [F6]. Hence these integrals agree. The expectation functional $\Lambda(Y):=\mathbb E[Y]=\langle Y,1\rangle_{L^2}$ is bounded since $|\Lambda(Y)|=|\langle Y,1\rangle_{L^2}|\le\|Y\|_2\|1\|_2=\|Y\|_2$. Applying the bounded-linear-map clause of [F6] gives $\mathbb E[X_T]=\int_0^T\mathbb E[J(t)]\,dt=0$, so $\operatorname{Var}(X_T)=\mathbb E[X_T^2]$.

The spatially normalized current convention is fixed by [F1]. In the quantum alternative, [A1] and [F2] apply to the exact $\alpha_t$, invariant state $\phi$, and centered self-adjoint $V$ in the Statement, so the supplier gives the variance identity and limit. The evenness asserted in the Statement follows from $C(-t)=\operatorname{Re}\phi(V\alpha_{-t}(V))=\operatorname{Re}\phi(\alpha_t(V)V)=\operatorname{Re}\overline{\phi(V\alpha_t(V))}=C(t)$, using invariance and self-adjointness. In the classical alternative, continuity of the inner product makes $(s,t)\mapsto\mathbb E[J(s)J(t)]=C(t-s)$ continuous on $[0,T]^2$. Riemann sums for $X_T$ converge in $L^2$, so continuity of the inner product makes the expectations of their squared norms converge to $\mathbb E[X_T^2]$; each squared-sum expectation is a product Riemann sum for this continuous kernel. Thus [F3] gives $\mathbb E[X_T^2]=\int_0^T\int_0^T C(t-s)\,ds\,dt$, which equals $\operatorname{Var}(X_T)$ by step 1.1. The integrand is symmetric because $C$ is even. The diagonal has zero area: it lies in strips of width $\delta$ and area at most $2T\delta+\delta^2$, tending to zero, so a bounded continuous integrand contributes zero there. Off the diagonal the two triangular restrictions are continuous; on a grid meeting the diagonal their upper-lower gap is bounded by the kernel oscillation away from the diagonal plus twice its supremum times the diagonal-strip area. Hence the product of the triangular indicator with the kernel is Riemann integrable. Each section has at most one jump and is therefore Riemann integrable. For the upper triangle, $g(t):=\int_0^t C(t-s)\,ds$ satisfies $|g(t)-g(t\prime)|\le T\omega_C(|t-t\prime|)+\|C\|_\infty|t-t\prime|$, where $\omega_C(\delta):=\sup_{|u-v|\le\delta}|C(u)-C(v)|\to0$; hence its outer integral is continuous. The lower triangle has the same estimate with reversed limits. Splitting the square into its two triangles and applying [F3] to each gives $2\int_0^T\int_0^t C(t-s)\,ds\,dt$.

For the classical alternative, apply [F4] to $\varphi(s)=t-s$ on $[0,t]$. It gives $\int_t^0 C(u)\,du=-\int_0^t C(t-s)\,ds$; reversing the oriented endpoints yields $\int_0^t C(t-s)\,ds=F(t)$, where $F(t):=\int_0^t C(u)\,du$. By [F7], $F'=C$; the product rule gives $(tF(t))'=F(t)+tC(t)$, a continuous derivative. Applying [F5] to $tF(t)$ and using $F(T)=\int_0^T C(u)\,du$ yields $\int_0^T F(t)\,dt=\int_0^T(T-u)C(u)\,du$. $$\left|\int_0^T(1-u/T)C(u)\,du-\int_0^\infty C(u)\,du\right|\le\frac{R}{T}K+2\int_R^\infty|C(u)|\,du.$$
First choose $R$ so the tail is arbitrarily small, then let $T\to\infty$; this proves the classical limit. The quantum limit is supplied by [F2].

In the classical alternative every finite-time variance is nonnegative, so its limit is nonnegative; in the quantum alternative nonnegativity is part of [F2]. The limit therefore has the stated sign in either case.

Fix either a finite open chain with sites $\{1,\ldots,L\}$, $L\ge2$, or a periodic chain with sites $\mathbb Z/L\mathbb Z$, $L\ge3$, and denote its site set by $\Lambda_L$. Let $\mathcal H_L$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space. For each site $j$, let $q_j=q_j^*$ be a bounded charge observable, with physical unit $\mathsf Q$. For each oriented nearest-neighbor bond $(j,j+1)$, let $h_{j,j+1}=h_{j,j+1}^*$ be an energy operator in joules. Require $[h_{k,k+1},q_j]=0$ whenever $j\notin\{k,k+1\}$, and require local charge conservation $[h_{j,j+1},q_j+q_{j+1}]=0$. On an open chain set $H_L=\sum_{j=1}^{L-1}h_{j,j+1}$; on a ring set $H_L=\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z/L\mathbb Z}h_{j,j+1}$ with periodic indices. For an open chain define the absent boundary currents $j_{0,1}=j_{L,L+1}=0$. Use $\hbar>0$ in joule-seconds. These finite local data may be realized on a tensor-product spin space or on a finite fixed-particle site space, provided the stated commutation conditions hold.

The oriented bond current from $j$ to $j+1$ is
$$j_{j,j+1}:=\frac{i}{\hbar}[h_{j,j+1},q_{j+1}].$$
It has unit $\mathsf Q\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$. The total current is the sum over existing bonds, $J_L:=\sum_{(j,j+1)}j_{j,j+1}$, and its Heisenberg evolution for $t\in\mathbb R$ is $J_L(t):=e^{iH_Lt/\hbar}J_Le^{-iH_Lt/\hbar}$. For finite inverse temperature $\beta>0$ in joules$^{-1}$, define $\rho_{\beta,L}:=e^{-\beta H_L}/\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta H_L})$ and $\omega_{\beta,L}(A):=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_{\beta,L}A)$. Write $J_L^\circ:=J_L-\omega_{\beta,L}(J_L)I$ and $J_L^\circ(t):=e^{iH_Lt/\hbar}J_L^\circ e^{-iH_Lt/\hbar}$. Define the real, connected, symmetrized correlation per site by
$$C_L(t):=\frac{1}{L}\operatorname{Re}\,\omega_{\beta,L}\!\left(J_L^\circ(t)J_L^\circ\right)=\frac{1}{2L}\omega_{\beta,L}\!\left(J_L^\circ(t)J_L^\circ+J_L^\circ J_L^\circ(t)\right).$$
The correlation has unit $\mathsf Q^2\,\mathrm{s}^{-2}$ per site.

This definition assigns no transport coefficient by itself. Any proposed finite-volume or thermodynamic transport quantity must additionally state its time cutoff, frequency regulator (for example $e^{-\eta t}$ with $\eta>0$ in seconds$^{-1}$), spatial normalization, and the exact order in which $L\to\infty$, the time cutoff tends to infinity, and any regulator is removed. Existence of those limits is not part of this definition.

Let $X$ be a real vector space ([[def-vector-space]]) with a norm $\|\cdot\|$ ([[def-norm-and-normed-space]]) whose metric $d(x,y):=\|x-y\|$ is complete ([[def-complete-metric-space]]). Let $a<b$ be reals ([[def-interval]]) and let $g:[a,b]\to X$ be continuous ([[def-metric-continuity]]). For endpoints $c,d\in[a,b]$, set $\int_c^c g:=0_X$ and, when $c>d$, set $\int_c^d g:=-\int_d^c g$; for $c<d$ use the Riemann-sum construction below on the restriction to $[c,d]$. Then:

1. **Integral.** For every sequence of tagged partitions of $[a,b]$ whose mesh tends to $0$, the Riemann sums $\sum_i(t_{i+1}-t_i)\,g(s_i)$ converge in $X$; the limit, written $\int_a^b g$, is independent of the sequence, and
$$\Bigl\|\int_a^b g\Bigr\|\;\le\;(b-a)\sup_{t\in[a,b]}\|g(t)\| .$$
2. **Fundamental theorem.** The curve $G:[a,b]\to X$, $G(t):=\int_a^t g$, is well defined, satisfies $\|G(t)-G(s)\|\le(t-s)\sup_{[s,t]}\|g\|$ for $a\le s\le t\le b$, and is differentiable with $G'=g$ on $[a,b]$ in the one-sided sense at the endpoints.
3. **Linearity.** For continuous $g,h:[a,b]\to X$ and reals $\alpha,\beta$: $\int_a^b(\alpha g+\beta h)=\alpha\int_a^b g+\beta\int_a^b h$; and for $a\le c\le b$, $\int_a^b g=\int_a^c g+\int_c^b g$.
4. **Bounded linear images.** If $Y$ is a normed real vector space and $T:X\to Y$ is linear with $\|Tx\|\le C\|x\|$ for some $C<+\infty$ and all $x$, then $T\circ g$ is continuous and $T\bigl(\int_a^b g\bigr)=\int_a^b (T\circ g)$; in particular, for every real-linear functional $\Lambda:X\to\mathbb R$ with $|\Lambda x|\le C\|x\|$, $\Lambda\bigl(\int_a^b g\bigr)=\int_a^b\Lambda\circ g$.

Fix either a finite open chain with sites $\{1,\ldots,L\}$, $L\ge2$, or a periodic chain with sites $\mathbb Z/L\mathbb Z$, $L\ge3$, and denote its site set by $\Lambda_L$. Let $\mathcal H_L$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space. For each site $j$, let $q_j=q_j^*$ be a bounded charge observable, with physical unit $\mathsf Q$. For each oriented nearest-neighbor bond $(j,j+1)$, let $h_{j,j+1}=h_{j,j+1}^*$ be an energy operator in joules. Require $[h_{k,k+1},q_j]=0$ whenever $j\notin\{k,k+1\}$, and require local charge conservation $[h_{j,j+1},q_j+q_{j+1}]=0$. On an open chain set $H_L=\sum_{j=1}^{L-1}h_{j,j+1}$; on a ring set $H_L=\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z/L\mathbb Z}h_{j,j+1}$ with periodic indices. For an open chain define the absent boundary currents $j_{0,1}=j_{L,L+1}=0$. Use $\hbar>0$ in joule-seconds. These finite local data may be realized on a tensor-product spin space or on a finite fixed-particle site space, provided the stated commutation conditions hold.

The oriented bond current from $j$ to $j+1$ is
$$j_{j,j+1}:=\frac{i}{\hbar}[h_{j,j+1},q_{j+1}].$$
It has unit $\mathsf Q\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$. The total current is the sum over existing bonds, $J_L:=\sum_{(j,j+1)}j_{j,j+1}$, and its Heisenberg evolution for $t\in\mathbb R$ is $J_L(t):=e^{iH_Lt/\hbar}J_Le^{-iH_Lt/\hbar}$. For finite inverse temperature $\beta>0$ in joules$^{-1}$, define $\rho_{\beta,L}:=e^{-\beta H_L}/\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta H_L})$ and $\omega_{\beta,L}(A):=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_{\beta,L}A)$. Write $J_L^\circ:=J_L-\omega_{\beta,L}(J_L)I$ and $J_L^\circ(t):=e^{iH_Lt/\hbar}J_L^\circ e^{-iH_Lt/\hbar}$. Define the real, connected, symmetrized correlation per site by
$$C_L(t):=\frac{1}{L}\operatorname{Re}\,\omega_{\beta,L}\!\left(J_L^\circ(t)J_L^\circ\right)=\frac{1}{2L}\omega_{\beta,L}\!\left(J_L^\circ(t)J_L^\circ+J_L^\circ J_L^\circ(t)\right).$$
The correlation has unit $\mathsf Q^2\,\mathrm{s}^{-2}$ per site.

This definition assigns no transport coefficient by itself. Any proposed finite-volume or thermodynamic transport quantity must additionally state its time cutoff, frequency regulator (for example $e^{-\eta t}$ with $\eta>0$ in seconds$^{-1}$), spatial normalization, and the exact order in which $L\to\infty$, the time cutoff tends to infinity, and any regulator is removed. Existence of those limits is not part of this definition.

Use the finite open or periodic chain and bond-current definition in [[def-qsmx-lattice-current-and-limits]]. Each $j_{j,j+1}$ is self-adjoint, and with $\dot q_j:=(i/\hbar)[H_L,q_j]$ the exact local identity
$$\dot q_j=j_{j-1,j}-j_{j,j+1}$$
holds at every site. Consequently the total charge $Q_L:=\sum_{j\in\Lambda_L}q_j$, where $\Lambda_L$ is the open-chain site set or periodic site set from the definition, is conserved: $[H_L,Q_L]=0$. The current orientation is from $j$ to $j+1$, so positive outgoing current lowers the charge at site $j$.

Take the finite-chain data of the current definition on $\mathcal H_L$ and identify $\mathcal H:=\mathcal H_L$. Let $H=H^*$ have energy unit joules, let $\hbar>0$ have unit joule-seconds, and let $\rho$ be a positive-definite trace-one matrix satisfying $[\rho,H]=0$. Define $\omega(A):=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho A)$ and $\alpha_t(A):=e^{iHt/\hbar}Ae^{-iHt/\hbar}$. Let $J_L$ be the total lattice current of the finite-volume current definition and center it with respect to this same $\rho$, setting $J:=J_L-\omega(J_L)I$. With no identification of $H$ and $H_L$, the estimate below is an abstract bound for this observable under $\alpha_t$. Its lattice-transport specialization further takes $H=H_L$; then the Gibbs density $\rho_{\beta,L}$ in that definition is stationary and is an admissible choice of $\rho$. More generally, $\rho_{\beta,L}$ can be used with another $H$ exactly when it also satisfies $[\rho_{\beta,L},H]=0$. Then $J=J^*$, as established by the local continuity result. For $m\ge1$, let $Q_1,\ldots,Q_m$ be linearly independent conserved matrices, $[H,Q_a]=0$. Put
$$G_{ab}:=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho Q_a^*Q_b),\qquad v_a:=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho Q_a^*J).$$
Then $G$ is positive definite, the finite Cesàro limit exists, and
$$\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac1T\int_0^T\operatorname{Re}\,\omega\!\left(\alpha_t(J)J\right)\,dt\;\ge\;v^*G^{-1}v\;\ge0.$$

Fix either a finite open chain with sites $\{1,\ldots,L\}$, $L\ge2$, or a periodic chain with sites $\mathbb Z/L\mathbb Z$, $L\ge3$, and denote its site set by $\Lambda_L$. Let $\mathcal H_L$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space. For each site $j$, let $q_j=q_j^*$ be a bounded charge observable, with physical unit $\mathsf Q$. For each oriented nearest-neighbor bond $(j,j+1)$, let $h_{j,j+1}=h_{j,j+1}^*$ be an energy operator in joules. Require $[h_{k,k+1},q_j]=0$ whenever $j\notin\{k,k+1\}$, and require local charge conservation $[h_{j,j+1},q_j+q_{j+1}]=0$. On an open chain set $H_L=\sum_{j=1}^{L-1}h_{j,j+1}$; on a ring set $H_L=\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z/L\mathbb Z}h_{j,j+1}$ with periodic indices. For an open chain define the absent boundary currents $j_{0,1}=j_{L,L+1}=0$. Use $\hbar>0$ in joule-seconds. These finite local data may be realized on a tensor-product spin space or on a finite fixed-particle site space, provided the stated commutation conditions hold.

The oriented bond current from $j$ to $j+1$ is
$$j_{j,j+1}:=\frac{i}{\hbar}[h_{j,j+1},q_{j+1}].$$
It has unit $\mathsf Q\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$. The total current is the sum over existing bonds, $J_L:=\sum_{(j,j+1)}j_{j,j+1}$, and its Heisenberg evolution for $t\in\mathbb R$ is $J_L(t):=e^{iH_Lt/\hbar}J_Le^{-iH_Lt/\hbar}$. For finite inverse temperature $\beta>0$ in joules$^{-1}$, define $\rho_{\beta,L}:=e^{-\beta H_L}/\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta H_L})$ and $\omega_{\beta,L}(A):=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_{\beta,L}A)$. Write $J_L^\circ:=J_L-\omega_{\beta,L}(J_L)I$ and $J_L^\circ(t):=e^{iH_Lt/\hbar}J_L^\circ e^{-iH_Lt/\hbar}$. Define the real, connected, symmetrized correlation per site by
$$C_L(t):=\frac{1}{L}\operatorname{Re}\,\omega_{\beta,L}\!\left(J_L^\circ(t)J_L^\circ\right)=\frac{1}{2L}\omega_{\beta,L}\!\left(J_L^\circ(t)J_L^\circ+J_L^\circ J_L^\circ(t)\right).$$
The correlation has unit $\mathsf Q^2\,\mathrm{s}^{-2}$ per site.

This definition assigns no transport coefficient by itself. Any proposed finite-volume or thermodynamic transport quantity must additionally state its time cutoff, frequency regulator (for example $e^{-\eta t}$ with $\eta>0$ in seconds$^{-1}$), spatial normalization, and the exact order in which $L\to\infty$, the time cutoff tends to infinity, and any regulator is removed. Existence of those limits is not part of this definition.
